correctness.rationale: Independent integer-pair arithmetic in Q(√5) reproduced the 30 edges, 20 triangular faces, no triple concurrence, 32 distinct sign patterns and all relevant midpoint incidences. Six general-position great circles have 32 chambers; their 12 vertex-ray and 20 facet-ray representatives give respectively 10 and 12 crossed edges, one section vertex per crossed edge. About a supporting vertex q the five ring neighbors are equally spaced at dot product 1/√5, and the other vertices are their antipodes and −q. The inner chamber is bounded by the five positive neighbor tests (their sum implies u·q>0); the Voronoi pentagon is bounded by their five bisectors. The other bisectors are at distances at least π/2−b>B(b) and do not clip it. Each normalized q+w gives a distinct inner vertex and outer side midpoint, so convexity gives nesting. In the hemisphere around q, a side at angular distance h removes the azimuth interval of half-length arccos(tan h cot t) at radius t; the five removed intervals first meet at half-length π/5. Integrating against sin t and differentiating the proposed L verifies the lens expression with zero at t=h. This gives the two joint cap areas and the factor 12/(4π); spherical excess of the inner pentagon gives its stated mass. In the overlap cos b<z<cos a, the outer cap has width density 2π in area units, while the positive inner density is 2π−10 arccos(z tan a/√(1−z²)), strictly smaller. The exclusive ends and minimum possible width follow from the respective inradii and circumradii, including B(a)=b and cos B(b)=√((5+2√5)/15). Exceptional section/width ties have zero Haar area.

originality.rationale: The distinctive claim is the elementary same-normal (central-section count, width) law and its type-separated thresholds, not either marginal. Earlier sources already give both marginals and their separate spherical descriptions, including the outer width pentagon and its transition value, but their displayed results do not compare the pentagons by orientation, identify their exact midpoint inclusion, or furnish both type-conditioned survival laws. The same-day joint shadow–section record has a different first observable and does not establish the width coupling. This is a bounded statement-level assessment, not a priority certificate.
residual_risks: Priority elsewhere in specialized geometric probability remains open; an unsuccessful focused search is not evidence of absence. Same-day order is not established, though the matching record's variables differ.
